units.title: Continuous sample paths give continuous marginal laws
units.statement: Let \(\rho_t\) be the pushforward law of the random state at time \(t\). Almost-sure continuity of whole sample paths implies continuity of the map from time to marginal law in the topology of integration against bounded continuous tests.
units.formula: t\mapsto\rho_t,\qquad \rho_t=(X_t)_\#P,\qquad t\mapsto\int g\,d\rho_t\text{ is continuous for every bounded continuous }g.
assumptions: Time ranges over a first-countable topological space. The sample law \(P\) is a probability measure on a measurable space.
The state space is topological and measurable, with measurable open sets. Each time slice \(X_t\) is measurable.
There is a single full-measure event on which each time path is continuous on the entire time space.

steps.title: Fix a time and use path continuity
steps.text: At any fixed time, the almost-sure path condition implies convergence to the state at that time as the time parameter approaches it.
steps.lean:
rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
  intro t
  have hae : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(μ : Measure Ω),
      Tendsto (fun u => X u ω) (𝓝 t) (𝓝 (X t ω)) :=
    hpaths.mono fun _ hω => hω.continuousAt.tendsto

steps.title: Pass to the laws
steps.text: The convergence-in-distribution theorem passes this almost-sure limit through bounded continuous tests. First countability gives a countably generated neighborhood filter.

units.lean_statement: Continuity is asserted for the actual time-slice pushforward law.
units.lean_proof: The proof uses convergence in distribution at each time.
units.boundary: The conclusion is continuity in the weak topology of probability measures.
tests: Focused Lean 4.33.0 compilation and axiom audit.

units.title: Marginal balance from a centered sample increment
units.statement: For each time \(v\), let \(\rho_v=(X_v)_\#P\). A sample increment equal almost surely to a signed time integral plus an integrable centered residual gives the following balance for the marginal expectations.
assumptions: The sample law \(P\) is a probability measure and the state space is measurable. Each slice \(X_v\) is measurable for every real \(v\).
The real test \(g\) is measurable. For each time \(v\), the state section \(A(v,\cdot)\) is measurable. The two random variables \(g(X_a)\) and \(g(X_b)\) are integrable.
The map \((v,\omega)\mapsto A(v,X_v(\omega))\) is integrable for the time-first product of Lebesgue measure restricted to \((\min(a,b),\max(a,b)]\) and \(P\).
The endpoints \(a,b\) are arbitrary reals. The signed integral identity \(g(X_b)-g(X_a)=\int_a^b A(v,X_v)\,dv+Z\) holds almost surely, where \(Z\) is integrable with expectation zero.
Product integrability gives integrable spatial drift sections for almost every restricted time. Spatial integrals use Lean's totalized Bochner convention at any exceptional time.

steps.title: Write marginal integrals as expectations
steps.text: The pushforward integral formula identifies each integral over the state law with the sample expectation of the composed test.
steps.lean:
have hmap (v : ℝ) {f : E → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) :
      (∫ x, f x ∂(μ.map (hX v).aemeasurable : Measure E)) =
        ∫ ω, f (X v ω) ∂(μ : Measure Ω) := by
    rw [ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map]
    exact integral_map (hX v).aemeasurable hf.aestronglyMeasurable

steps.title: Integrate the signed time sections
steps.text: Product integrability gives an integrable sample function by Fubini. The integral reverses sign when the endpoints reverse.
steps.lean:
let D : Ω → ℝ := fun ω => ∫ v in a..b, A v (X v ω)
  have hD : Integrable D (μ : Measure Ω) := by
    have hI := hdrift.swap.integral_prod_left
    change Integrable (fun ω => ∫ v in Set.uIoc a b, A v (X v ω)) (μ : Measure Ω) at hI
    by_cases hab : a ≤ b
    · simpa only [D, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab, Set.uIoc_of_le hab] using hI
    · have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_not_ge hab
      simpa only [D, intervalIntegral.integral_of_ge hba, Set.uIoc_of_ge hba] using hI.fun_neg

steps.title: Center and exchange integrations
steps.text: Take expectations of the sample identity and use centering to remove the residual. Exchange expectation and signed time integration, then express the expectation through each marginal law.
steps.lean:
rw [hmap b hg, hmap a hg, ← integral_sub hgb hga, integral_congr_ae hinc,
    integral_add hD hZ, hmean, add_zero]
  simp_rw [hmap _ (hA _)]
  exact (intervalIntegral_integral_swap hdrift).symm

units.lean_statement: The hypothesis uses restricted time-first product integrability and allows either endpoint order.
units.lean_proof: The proof uses the pushforward formula and Fubini for signed interval integrals.
units.boundary: The sample increment identity and the centered residual are supplied.
tests: Focused Lean 4.33.0 compilation and axiom audit.

units.title: Differentiating a local marginal balance
units.statement: For a weakly continuous curve of laws \(\rho_t\), set \(F(t)=\int g\,d\rho_t\) and \(B(t)=\int A(t,x)\,d\rho_t(x)\). A local signed balance about \(s\) gives the ordinary derivative of \(F\) at \(s\).
assumptions: The state space is compact and topological with measurable open sets. The curve \(t\mapsto\rho_t\) consists of probability laws, is defined for real times, and is weakly continuous.

The scalar field \(A\) is jointly continuous on real time times state. The function \(g\) is real-valued, and the statement uses Lean's totalized Bochner integral. The given balance uses those same integrals.
The signed balance holds for all \(u\) in a neighborhood of the real time \(s\).

steps.title: Use continuity of the averaged field
steps.text: Compactness of the state and weak continuity of the laws let us integrate the jointly continuous time-dependent field continuously.
steps.lean:
let B := fun v => ∫ x, A v x ∂(μ v : Measure E)
  have hB : Continuous B := continuous_integral_of_compact hA hμ

steps.title: Differentiate the primitive
steps.text: The ordinary interval fundamental theorem gives derivative \(B(s)\) for the integral with fixed lower endpoint \(s\).
steps.lean:
have hprimitive : HasDerivAt (fun u => ∫ v in s..u, B v) (B s) s :=
    intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right (hB.intervalIntegrable s s)
      hB.stronglyMeasurable.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter hB.continuousAt

steps.title: Use the balance in a neighborhood
steps.text: Adding \(F(s)\) to the primitive gives a function equal to \(F\) near \(s\), so the same derivative applies.
steps.lean:
apply (hprimitive.const_add (∫ x, g x ∂(μ s : Measure E))).congr_of_eventuallyEq
  filter_upwards [hbalance] with u hu
  change (∫ x, g x ∂(μ u : Measure E)) =
    (∫ x, g x ∂(μ s : Measure E)) + ∫ v in s..u, B v
  exact eq_add_of_sub_eq' hu

units.lean_statement: The premise is a neighborhood equality of the same integral expression used in the conclusion.
units.lean_proof: The proof uses continuity of the averaged field and transfers the derivative by local equality.
units.boundary: This is the pointwise derivative under a jointly continuous field and a local balance on the real line.
tests: Focused Lean 4.33.0 compilation and axiom audit.

units.title: Bounded measurable coefficients along progressive paths
units.statement: The scalar process \(b(t,\omega)=c(t,X_t(\omega))\) is strongly progressive. Its time section is integrable for every sample on the specified horizon and it has the indicated product-space \(L^p\) membership.
assumptions: The state space is pseudometrizable with its Borel measurable structure. The sample measure \(\mu\) is finite and its filtration is indexed by nonnegative time.

The process \(X\) is jointly measurable and strongly progressive. The real coefficient \(c\) on nonnegative time times state is Borel measurable. A finite constant bounds \(|c(t,w)|\) for all \(t\le T\) and all states \(w\).
The horizon \(T\) is nonnegative and \(p\) is any extended nonnegative real exponent.
The symbol \(\ell_T\) denotes Lebesgue time restricted to \([0,T]\).

steps.title: Compose on each restricted filtration product
steps.text: The pair \((t,X_t)\) is measurable on each time prefix for that prefix's sigma-algebra. Real-valued Borel measurability gives strong measurability.
steps.lean:
· intro t
    let _ : MeasurableSpace Ω := filtration t
    exact (hc.comp
      ((measurable_subtype_coe.comp measurable_fst).prodMk (hProgressive t).measurable)).stronglyMeasurable
steps.detail: Use strong progressiveness and measurable composition on the restricted domain.

steps.title: Apply the pointwise bound
steps.text: The finite horizon measure is supported in the specified interval. On the product the same time-coordinate bound holds almost everywhere, and both measures are finite.
steps.lean:
· intro ω
    have hm := hc.comp (measurable_id.prodMk
      (hX.comp (measurable_id.prodMk (measurable_const (a := ω)))))
    exact Integrable.of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C
      (htime.mono fun t ht => hC t ht (X t ω))
  · have hXswap : Measurable (fun z : Ω × ℝ≥0 => X z.2 z.1) :=
      hX.comp (measurable_snd.prodMk measurable_fst)
    have hm := hc.comp (measurable_snd.prodMk hXswap)
    change MemLp (processFunction b) p (μ.prod (TimeMeasure.upTo T))
    exact MemLp.of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C
      ((Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd.ae htime).mono fun z hz => hC z.2 hz (X z.2 z.1))

units.lean_statement: The product measure is ordered sample first and time second.
units.lean_proof: The proof composes on the filtration prefixes and bounds the resulting sections.
units.boundary: The coefficient bound is pointwise on the selected horizon, which yields time integrability at every sample.
tests: Focused local Lean 4.33.0 compilation and axiom audit.

units.title: From centered increments to a two-time marginal balance
units.statement: Write \(\rho_t=(X_t)_\#P\). On the real time axis put \(F(t)=\int g\,d\rho_{t^+}\) and \(B(t)=\int A(t^+,w)\,d\rho_{t^+}(w)\), with \(t^+=\max(t,0)\). Then \(B\) is locally Lebesgue integrable, and \(F\) is absolutely continuous on every finite nonnegative interval and satisfies the displayed identities.
assumptions: The state space is compact and second countable with its Borel measurable structure. The sample measure \(P\) is a probability measure. The state process \(X\) is jointly measurable and the real test \(g\) is continuous.
The scalar field \(A\) is jointly measurable. For each \(T\ge0\) one finite constant bounds \(|A(t,w)|\) for every \(0\le t\le T\) and every state \(w\).

For each nonnegative \(t\), on a full-measure event for that time, \(g(X_t)-g(X_0)=\int_0^t A(v,X_v)\,dv+Z_t\), where \(Z_t\) is integrable and has expectation zero. Both endpoints \(a,b\) in the conclusion are arbitrary nonnegative times, with the signed integral convention.

steps.title: Take expectations
steps.text: On each bounded horizon the generator along the process is jointly measurable and bounded. Use Fubini and change variables under the time-slice pushforward.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨Z, hZi, hmean, hZ⟩ := hbalance t
    have hinc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω),
        g (Y t ω) - g (Y 0 ω) =
          (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), A' v (Y v ω)) + Z ω := by
      simpa [Y, A'] using hZ
    have h := weak_integral_balance_of_centered_increment P Y hY hg.measurable hAsection
      0 (t : ℝ) (hgi 0) (hgi t) hGi hZi hmean hinc
    exact eq_add_of_sub_eq' h

steps.title: Recover the two-time identity and absolute continuity
steps.text: Subtract the balances at the two endpoints. The local uniform bound transfers to \(B\) and makes its primitive Lipschitz on each finite horizon.
steps.lean:
have hTwo (a b : ℝ≥0) : F b - F a = ∫ v in (a : ℝ)..(b : ℝ), B v := by
    rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_left (hInt 0 b) (hInt 0 a), hBase a, hBase b]
    ring
  refine ⟨hLoc, hTwo, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro T
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hBbound T
    have hLip : LipschitzOnWith C F (Icc (0 : ℝ) (T : ℝ)) := by
      rw [lipschitzOnWith_iff_dist_le_mul]
      intro x hx y hy
      have h := hTwo y.toNNReal x.toNNReal
      rw [Real.coe_toNNReal y hy.1, Real.coe_toNNReal x hx.1] at h
      have hBoundI : ∀ v ∈ uIoc y x, ‖B v‖ ≤ C := by
        intro v hv
        have hu : v ∈ uIcc y x := uIoc_subset_uIcc hv
        have hvT : v ≤ (T : ℝ) := hu.2.trans (max_le hy.2 hx.2)
        exact hC v (by simpa using Real.toNNReal_le_toNNReal hvT)
      rw [Real.dist_eq, h, ← Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.dist_eq]
      exact intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const hBoundI
    apply LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval
    rwa [uIcc_of_le T.coe_nonneg]

steps.title: Differentiate the primitive almost everywhere
steps.text: Lebesgue differentiation applies to the locally integrable extension of \(B\). Near each positive time the primitive plus the initial constant agrees with \(F\).
steps.lean:
· have hPositive : ∀ᵐ t ∂volume.restrict (Ioi (0 : ℝ)), 0 < t :=
      ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioi
    filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae (LocallyIntegrable.ae_hasDerivAt_integral hLoc), hPositive] with t ht ht0
    apply ((ht 0).const_add (F 0)).congr_of_eventuallyEq
    filter_upwards [Ioi_mem_nhds ht0] with r hr
    have h := hBase r.toNNReal
    simpa only [Real.coe_toNNReal r hr.le] using h
steps.detail: Use LocallyIntegrable.ae_hasDerivAt_integral and local equality on positive time.

units.lean_statement: The real extensions of the pushforward expectations use nonnegative time.
units.lean_proof: The proof combines the centered weak balance with Lebesgue differentiation.
units.boundary: The ordinary derivative assertion holds for Lebesgue-almost every strictly positive real time.
tests: Focused local Lean 4.33.0 compilation and axiom audit.
